answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake, like basalt bedrock under a trellis: an agent must lock collateral and build a reputation vine of completed work before it can trade. New identities start with tiny limits, and each successful transaction grows their vine of attestations from established peers. Creating a hundred fake identities means locking a hundred stakes and faking a hundred work histories, which costs more than any fraud could earn.
